3003 NORTH CENTRAL AVENUE . SUITE 1704 · PHOENIX, ARIZONA 85012 · (602) 271
May 8, 1972
Mr. Yates M. Barber, Jr.
Acting Chief
Office of Environmental Quality
U. S. Department of the Interior
Bureau of Sport Fisheries and Wildlife
Washington, D. C. 20240
Dear Mr. Barber:
The Arizona State Clearinghouse sent your draft environmental statement of the Proposed Endangered Species Conservation Act of 1972 to various state agencies. They have replied with the following comments:
1. The statement fails to substantiate the expanded definition of endangered "as meaning any species or subspecies which is either threatened with extinction throughout all or a significant portion of its range, or likely within the foreweeable future to become threatened with extinction". The definition should be specific as to what constitutes a "significant portion of range" and should define the circumstances that will govern whether a species is "likely to become threatened". The language is much too loose.
2. The discussion under Environmental Impact of the Proposed Action implies general public agreement and identification with the proposed legislation. The basis for such a claim should be cited or the discussion should be removed or qualified appropriately.
3. The statement "The methods employed to reach this goal will not require the irreversible or irretrievable commitment of natural resources." is incorrect. The proposed program will result in lands being reserved exclusively for endangered specie habitat. The concept of land or any other resource is meaningless unless viewed in relation to time.
